messages.author: 8c2e87775d0eb60c
messages.subject: Odd results in collostructional analysis
parts:
Dear all, 

I'm doing an analysis on at-constructions using the R scripts for collostructional analysis (verbs in A-construction). The issue comes from the different results I've obtained with the "old" script (coll.analysis 3.2a) and the new one. In the first case, some verbs returned "inf" results for FYE, those that were situated at the top of the list ordered by Coll.Strength, which was logical because the ratio between Word in A/Word in Corpus was the higher (the so-called "faith" in the output file). So, in order to get rid of those "inf" results I applied the new script (mpfr-based) setting the default argument (3), and  also I tried with the recommended option (4) (when I set argument (5) the script froze). Then, with the new script the verb that was on the top of the list with an "inf" Coll.Strength is now situated at the end of those showing "attraction" because the FYE result is NA. The values for the intermediate calculations are the same in the three cases, but I guess that the previous "inf" result is given now an error because somewhere the value is too low that it is taken as zero in the -log() calculation. I've attached the results for this verb with the two scripts.
Is there any solution to get a "logical" FYE result for this verb? Am I correct  interpreting the results in this way?

Thanks very much!!!

It returns NaN with precbitsexponent=3, 4, and 5 (with precbitsexponent=4, the script needed maybe 7 minutes or so and the R instance required about 4.2 GB of RAM). I am currently looking into where the error comes from - right now, I can see that the NaN at least originates in hypergeom.mpfr ,but it may take me a while to get to the bottom of this so my recommendation for now would be to just use LLR as the measure of collocational strength because its computation won't collapse and it's so highly correlated with FYE that the results are most of the time not different enough.

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Odd results in collostructional analysis
parts:
Hi Soluna

Ok, so I isolated the problem ... It's not a mistake in the script, as
far as I can tell, but it's really just that the numbers involved are
just too huge. FYE is based on adding up probabilities computed from
the hypergeometric distribution. Computing those in turn requires
binomial coefficients, which in your case amount to crazy high
numbers: c+d over c and n over a+c involve values approaching 1E+8 in
your case. The Rmpfr library should be able to handle this, but it
just takes forever and requires so much RAM that it doesn't complete
on a normal computer with, I dunno, 16GB RAM. Now, I did write a
function that can maybe handle this, but it's a nightmare because I
basically made it cancel fractions before multiplication to reduce the
super-high products, but you can see where this is going ... use LLR
;-)

Cheers,

STG

messages.author: 97ce067823027f53
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Odd results in collostructional analysis
parts:
Could you compute everything on the log scale, then exponentiate at the end? That should avoid the blow-up. Most distributions have a log option, such as dhyper(…, log = TRUE). To sum up log probabilities, you can use an identity: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Log_probability#Addition_in_log_space

Here’s a quick example of summing log probs. You would replace something like log(x) with your real log probabilities, e.g. dhyper(blah, log = TRUE): https://gist.github.com/alexperrone/e72d7cf98944c82208ad04794e610117
